x: In the next event, the 2 Miles, we were represented by Speechley and Harley, whilst Surrey W.C. had Fisher and Burgess, the Kent champion. From the start Stone (Poly.) led, followed by the Surrey pair, and our two.

Of our non-scoring "A" team men, Green gained a first-class standard medal, and Harley and Urry second-class medals. Our "B" team acquitted themselves well in finishing 12th of the 17 teams to close in.

Percy Wright walked well at his first attempt, but was leg-weary towards the end and was passed by Harley, who won the sealed handicap. As the result shows, Belgrave had a slight advantage over the Police in the match.

Churcher, Fletcher, Green, Harley, Readman and Rickards, should be our team. Unfortunately, Fletcher was indisposed, Green was unable to turn out, and Rickards was also compelled to stand down at the last moment.
The two miles race lacked interest and we were able to help our score along by placing the first two men. Don Brown had an "easy," and Harley was not seriously troubled in taking second position.
Bentley, Rickards, Snell, Harley, and Doubleday retired (and others).
Stone and Sons, Mr. and Mrs. Harley (Senior), Etienne Gailly, George Durrant, Derrick Burfitt, Norman Graves and the Wirral A.C.
Later in the year Harry won the HORWOOD CUP, with Redgrave second, Speechley third and Harley fourth----the first of many trophies he was to hold over the years.

Fifteen walkers contested the 2 miles championship, and from the starting shot Brown led, with Harley on his heels for 200 yards. The curtain rose at 9 pm with Miss Gladys Bailey singing "Over My Shoulder", which served to introduce us to "The Seven Belgrave Sisters" (including sylph-like Sidney and Harley, the original Harlequin) in a singing and dancing act which was well received.
